Simulate a bulk sample as a sum of single cells

Source: R/01_01_single_cell_toy_simulation.R
simulate_bulk_from_cells.Rd

Draws cell counts \(m_{\cdot i}\sim Multinomial(n_i,p_{\cdot i})\), then the exact Gaussian sum of those cells, \(T_{ji}\sim N(m_{ji}\mu_{\cdot j},m_{ji}\Sigma_{W,j})\), and scales the total by the platform factor: \(\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot i}=a_i\sum_j\boldsymbol{T}_{ji}\). A sum of \(m\) independent Gaussian cells is Gaussian, so there is no per-cell loop.

This is the single-cell mixture (covariance linear in the cell counts). simulate_bulk_mixture() remains the population-profile convolution, whose covariance is weighted by \(p_j^2\).

Pass the cellular moments (generative_mean, generative_sigma from rescale_single_cell_moments()), not a library-normalised reference. The returned estimand is the realised cell fraction \(\boldsymbol{m}_{\cdot i}/n_i\).

Usage

simulate_bulk_from_cells(
  mean_signature_matrix,
  Sigma,
  p,
  n_cells,
  platform_scale = 1,
  n_samples = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

mean_signature_matrix

Per-cell means \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}\) (\(G\times J\)).

Sigma

Per-cell covariances \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{W,j}\) (\(G\times G\times J\)).

p

Cell-fraction vector of length \(J\), or a \(J\times N\) matrix. Each column must sum to 1.

n_cells

Cells per bulk sample, \(n_i\). Recycled to \(N\). The multinomial size is the rounded value; the fitted \(\hat n\) need not be an integer.

platform_scale

Capture scale \(a_i\). Use 1 when the bulk and the single-cell platform share their scale, and 2 when the bulk captures twice as much transcript per cell. Recycled to \(N\).

n_samples

Number of bulk samples when p is a vector. Ignored when p already has one column per sample, unless it matches that number.

seed

Optional seed, passed to set.seed() before the draws.

Value

A list with Y (\(G\times N\)), nominal p, realised p_realised (\(\boldsymbol{m}/n\)), counts (\(\boldsymbol{m}\)), transcript fractions q, cell_size \(S_j=\mathbf{1}^{\top} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}\), platform_scale \(a\), n_cells \(n\), mean_scale \(c=an\) and variance_scale \(\phi=a^{2}n\).

See also

simulate_bulk_mixture(), rescale_single_cell_moments(), deconvolute_single_cell()

Examples

genes <- paste0("g", 1:4)
cts <- paste0("ct", 1:2)
mu <- matrix(
  c(2, 2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 3, 3),
  nrow = 4,
  dimnames = list(genes, cts)
)
sigma <- array(0, c(4, 4, 2), dimnames = list(genes, genes, cts))
sigma[,, 1] <- diag(0.05, 4)
sigma[,, 2] <- diag(0.05, 4)
set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_bulk_from_cells(
  mu,
  sigma,
  p = c(0.8, 0.2),
  n_cells = 2000,
  platform_scale = 2,
  n_samples = 2
)
colSums(sim$counts)
#> sample_1 sample_2 
#>     2000     2000
